content: Phenobarbital significantly reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of numerous drugs by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly through the cytochrome P450 enzyme system (e.g., CYP3A4, CYP1A2, CYP2C19) and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. This interaction often leads to decreased drug efficacy, potential therapeutic failure, and the development of resistance in certain cases. Below are the detailed interactions and clinical implications for specific drugs: 1. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Phenobarbital decreases the levels of these antimalarial agents by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced serum concentrations and loss of antimalarial efficacy. 2. Atazanavir: Phenobarbital reduces atazanavir levels by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to therapeutic failure and resistance. 3. Cabotegravir: Phenobarbital increases the metabolism of cabotegravir via UGT1A1 and UGT1A9 enzymes, reducing systemic exposure and virologic response. Co-administration is contraindicated. 4. Cariprazine: Phenobarbital decreases cariprazine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the unclear net effect and potential therapeutic failure. 5. Cobicistat-containing regimens: Phenobarbital reduces the efficacy of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 6. Darunavir: Phenobarbital decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 induction, leading to potential therapeutic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Phenobarbital reduces contraceptive efficacy by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should avoid using this combination during phenobarbital therapy and for at least 28 days after discontinuation of the inducer. 8. Doravirine: Phenobarbital reduces doravirine plasma concentrations via CYP3A4 induction, potentially leading to virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Phenobarbital reduces the therapeutic effect of these agents by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Phenobarbital decreases the levels of this combination therapy, leading to virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Etravirine: Phenobarbital increases the metabolism of etravirine, reducing its plasma levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Fostemsavir: Phenobarbital significantly decreases the active moiety (temsavir) plasma concentrations by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Phenobarbital reduces the levels of isavuconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Phenobarbital decreases sofosbuvir levels via P-glycoprotein induction, reducing its active metabolite and pharmacologic effect. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Lopinavir/Ritonavir: Phenobarbital reduces lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to therapeutic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Phenobarbital reduces ivacaftor exposure by 57%, potentially diminishing the effectiveness of this combination. Co-administration is not recommended. 17. Lurasidone: Phenobarbital decreases lurasidone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Mavacamten: Phenobarbital reduces mavacamten levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Naloxegol: Phenobarbital reduces naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is not recommended. 20. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: Phenobarbital significantly reduces nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations, leading to virologic failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir & Dasabuvir (DSC): Phenobarbital reduces the efficacy of this combination by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Panobinostat: Phenobarbital reduces panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Pirfenidone: Phenobarbital induces CYP1A2 metabolism, reducing pirfenidone levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Praziquantel: Phenobarbital reduces praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Regorafenib: Phenobarbital decreases regorafenib levels while increasing its active metabolite (M-5). Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Rilpivirine: Phenobarbital reduces rilpivirine levels, leading to virologic failure and resistance. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Roflumilast: Phenobarbital reduces roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 induction, diminishing its therapeutic effect. Co-administration is not recommended. 28. Sodium Oxybate: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases CNS depression, leading to profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Vandetanib: Phenobarbital reduces vandetanib exposure by up to 40% via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Voriconazole: Phenobarbital reduces voriconazole levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Abemaciclib: Phenobarbital reduces abemaciclib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 32. Acalabrutinib: Phenobarbital reduces acalabrutinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided or the dose adjusted. 33. Adagrasib: Phenobarbital reduces adagrasib levels via CYP3A4 induction, while adagrasib increases phenobarbital levels via CYP2C9 inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided. 34. Afatinib: Phenobarbital reduces afatinib levels via P-glycoprotein induction. Dose adjustments may be required if co-administration is necessary. 35. Alosetron: Phenobarbital reduces alosetron levels via CYP1A2 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. 36. Alpelisib: Phenobarbital reduces alpelisib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. 37. Antithrombin Alfa/III: Phenobarbital reduces the effects of antithrombin by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. 38. Apalutamide: Phenobarbital levels are reduced by apalutamide via CYP2C19 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. 39. Apixaban: Phenobarbital reduces apixaban levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Apremilast: Phenobarbital reduces apremilast levels via CYP3A4 induction, leading to potential therapeutic failure. Co-administration should be avoided. 41. Argatroban: Phenobarbital reduces argatroban levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. 42. Avapritinib: Phenobarbital reduces avapritinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. 43. Axitinib: Phenobarbital reduces axitinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. 44. Bedaquiline: Phenobarbital reduces bedaquiline levels via CYP3A4 induction, leading to reduced therapeutic efficacy. Co-administration should be avoided. 45. Bemiparin: Phenobarbital reduces bemiparin effects by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. 46. Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Co-administration with phenobarbital increases the risk of profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Co-administration should be avoided. 47. Bictegravir: Phenobarbital reduces bictegravir levels via CYP3A4 and UGT1A1 induction, leading to virologic failure. Co-administration should be avoided. 48. Bivalirudin: Phenobarbital reduces bivalirudin effects by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. 49. Bosutinib: Phenobarbital reduces bosutinib levels by approximately 85% via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. 50. Bremelanotide: Phenobarbital reduces bremelanotide levels. Co-administration should be avoided. In summary, phenobarbital's strong enzyme-inducing properties necessitate careful consideration of drug interactions to avoid therapeutic failure, resistance, or severe adverse effects. Alternative medications or dose adjustments should be considered when co-administration is unavoidable.
